objective: Make the owner-created ElevenLabs AI voice the default local Hina voice through fixed VieNeu reference enrollment, preserve supported Vietnamese expressive cues, and apply a bounded pitch-preserving speed-up to long replies.
non_goals: Do not claim that a new TTS model was trained or fine-tuned from one 51-second MP3.
Do not permit arbitrary uploaded voice cloning.
Do not retain generated speech or raw chat text.
Do not switch to a research-licensed 4B TTS model without a separate license and resource gate.
contracts: The only cloneable voice is the fixed owner-authorized Hina reference asset with recorded provenance and hash.
Reference enrollment remains in memory and never writes a user voice into the installed VieNeu package.
Supported cues are normalized to VieNeu v3 Turbo emotion tokens before inference; unsupported cues are removed rather than spoken literally.
Short utterances remain at normal speed and long utterances are accelerated only within a bounded 1.00x to 1.18x range.
All synthesized output continues through pre-TTS moderation and watermarking.
allowed_dependencies: Existing pinned VieNeu-TTS 3.2.3, NumPy and ONNX Runtime dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: The fixed Hina reference WAV is hash-bound and becomes the default VieNeu voice.
VieNeu enrollment downloads and loads the pinned speaker encoder and denoiser artifacts.
chuckles, laughs, sighs, takes a deep breath and clears throat aliases reach the supported VieNeu cue vocabulary.
Unsupported cues such as yawns and smacks lips are omitted without being spoken as words.
Unit tests cover consent binding, cue normalization, adaptive rate bounds and pitch-preserving output duration.
A real VieNeu CPU smoke produces a WAV using the Hina profile.
